First, we want to find the interval for $\theta $ that corresponds to the first petal. Since the curve bounding the region crosses itself at the origin, we want to find the values of $\theta $ for which $r=0$, or 

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )=0.
$$

This gives us two solutions for $5\theta \in [-\pi ,\pi ):$

$$
5\theta =0,\pi \,⟹\,\theta =0,\frac{\pi }{5}
$$

As a result, the first petal is traversed for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{5}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/6c35b0e3c4e51b164097e6deb11e4418726927f478f934e41d1250388e9a27e5.png)

Since there are $5$ petals, the total area bounded by the polar curve can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{\text{total}} & =5\cdot {A}_{\text{petal}} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{(4\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ))}^{2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =5\cdot \frac{16}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =40\cdot \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(10\theta ))\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =20{(\theta -\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(10\theta ))|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =20[(\frac{\pi }{5}-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi ))-(0-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))] \\  & =20\cdot \frac{\pi }{5} \\  & =4\pi \end{aligned}
$$
